prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Sentinel Vale: EO mission (land/coastal/cryosphere products, predictable latency, documented quality). External: spacecraft, launch segment, user processing environments, conjunction data source, users (registered/anonymous). Security: least privilege, strong auth, segmentation, continuous audit. Mission Control Center (Bluebell): real-time authority boundary, pass supervision, anomaly response, contact schedule, routing policy, command prep package from MPS; sends constraints to MPS; coordinates with PPF; elevated access tied to approved shift role + time-limited need. Uplink needs MCC + Spacecraft Operations Team concurrence. Command Validation Gateway (Osprey) validates command stacks; rejects unapproved/unprovenanced/expired/out-of-window items; accepts Star Tracker Mask File only if integrity, config ID, approval match security baseline. Cybersecurity Desk: exceptions, daily privileged-access review (dormant/shared accounts), reviews public interface changes; coordinates anomalies with suspicious auth/data movement/tampering. Flight Dynamics Facility (Mistral): orbit catalog; ephemerides/events to MCC, MPS, PPF; mask file; orbit quality state to archive queue. Flight Dynamics Team: maneuver/collision screening; maneuver recommendation to Spacecraft Operations Team; Ephemeris Delta Note; assesses orbit/timing anomalies. Orbit Determination Engine: Doppler Residual Report, Laser Retroreflector Window (MPS uses only in approved interval). Mission Planning System (Cedar): authoritative timeline. Network Control System (Lantern): enforces approved routing, logs config changes; Security Exception Ticket. Payload Processing Facility (Forgehouse): Primary/Backup Processing Clusters L0–L2; both down: suspend, preserve raw, notify MCC; delivers product package, quality metadata, checksums to archive. Telemetry Ingest Service: Pass Replay Packet → Spacecraft Operations Team (anomaly reconstruction). Payload Calibration Team: baseline, reprocessing requests, product-integrity triage. Product Quality Service: quality flags, Product Hold List, public status, records reprocessing reason. Long Term Archive (Granite): authoritative repository; persistent IDs; catalogue (baseline, sensing/publication time, quality, replacement links) to User Services Portal after PQS+embargo; Storage Watermark Snapshot; keeps replaced versions unless consolidation allowed; retention rules. User Services Portal: search/order/download, versioned contracts, subscriptions; status message on archive failure + incident. Anomaly classification: safety, command authority, custody, continuity, user commitments; SOT triages spacecraft, Ground Network Manager

New part:
S213: During triage, operators preserve volatile logs, current configuration state, operator console history, and relevant message identifiers before restarting services or changing routing.
S214: Evidence is stored in write-protected case storage with a chain of custody entry that identifies the collector, collection time, source system, and reason for capture.
S215: Forgehouse must quarantine suspect input and derived output when product lineage cannot be proven during an active anomaly investigation.
S216: Cedar suspends automatic schedule publication when a security or continuity anomaly could invalidate contact commitments or conflict with manual recovery actions.
S217: Continuity modes are declared by the Mission Control Center after consultation with the affected technical leads and are recorded with the operational objective, expected duration, and exit criteria.
S218: In monitor-only mode, command release is stopped, telemetry reception continues where safe, and engineering teams focus on stabilizing observability and protecting evidence.
S219: In essential-service mode, the ground segment prioritizes spacecraft safety contacts, time-critical telemetry capture, core orbit support, and protection of unrecoverable payload data.
S220: Primary Processing Cluster can pause nonessential production queues and reserve compute capacity for validated recovery runs from known-good inputs.
S221: If site degradation persists, processing work is transferred to Backup Processing Cluster only after input custody, software baseline, and operator authorization have been verified.
S222: Cross-site failover is coordinated through Ground Network Manager so that antenna allocation, network routing, firewall state, and contact schedules remain consistent.
S223: North S-Band Antenna, South S-Band Antenna, Kiruna X-Band Antenna, and Svalbard X-Band Antenna are placed in the recovery plan according to current availability and the spacecraft contact priority.
S224: Long Term Archive remains the custody reference during degraded operations, and any delayed ingest or publication is reconciled before normal service status is restored.
S225: User Services Portal communicates confirmed service impacts in operational terms and avoids publishing speculative root cause information before the incident lead approves release.
S226: Recovery is accepted only when command authority is verified, telemetry and product flows are reconciled, security monitoring has returned to the approved baseline, and responsible teams have signed the incident record.
S227: Routine mission service begins only after the operational readiness review confirms that ground procedures, staffing rosters, monitoring views, and escalation paths are under configuration control.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
